claims.text: implement parallelization in a general way so other indices like txindex can benefit
claims.quote: did you attempt to implement parallelization in a more general way so that other indices could benefit from it as well?
claims.status_note: author implemented generic workers pool and txindex parallelization

claims.text: separate parallelization and index logic so it can be reused across other indexes
claims.quote: Perhaps it could have separate parallelization and index logic. So it could be reused in other indexes.
claims.status_note: author separated generic ThreadPool in later push

claims.text: how parallel indexing interacts with AssumeUTXO (AU)
claims.quote: Also, how would this work with AU?

claims.text: spin down or destroy worker threads once initial index sync is complete
claims.quote: Maybe the threads should spin down if there's not much work.
claims.status_note: author agreed and destructed thread pool once initial sync completes
claims.status_by_quote: The thread pool can be destructed once all indexes initial sync finish

claims.text: taking a reference to a temporary CBlockUndo object at block height 0 causes undefined behavior
claims.quote: I'm not sure this is safe. It looks like if block height is 0 this is taking a reference to a temporary object that will go out scope.
claims.status_note: author agreed and simplified to Assert(block.undo_data)

claims.text: opportunistically run post-processing in worker threads to prevent idle threads
claims.quote: It seems like this idleness could be avoided by moving the CustomPostProcessBlocks calls into the worker threads. So that whenever each worker thread finishes processing blocks, it then opportunistically calls CustomPostProcessBlocks to post-process any blocks that are available
claims.status_note: implemented opportunistic post-processing pipeline in worker threads
claims.status_by_quote: Spent a few days implementing this suggestion... The process runs faster now.

claims.text: intermittent segfault during index sync caused by worker threads accessing an index Sync() local variable post-destruction
claims.quote: Fwiw I encountered a segfault previously while testing on master on previous PR HEAD
claims.status_note: author fixed subtle race condition where worker thread accessed destroyed local variable
claims.status_by_quote: There was a very subtle bug on which the worker threads might have accessed an index Sync() local variable post-destruction.

claims.text: thread pool fuzzer times out after 1608 seconds during thread destruction and joining
claims.quote: It seems to have found something: ... ERROR: libFuzzer: timeout after 1608 seconds
claims.status_note: author added fuzz harness and fixed shutdown synchronization bug
claims.status_by_quote: Updated with a fuzz test case from @TheCharlatan. Thanks!

claims.text: parallel indexing on HDDs causes a 2x slowdown compared to sequential master due to disk seek penalties without warning in help
claims.quote: observed a slowdown on a HDD compared to master (by a factor 2)... Should it be mentioned in the -indexworkers help
claims.status_note: author updated -indexworkers help documentation warning against HDD use

claims.text: whether ThreadPool should support assigning tasks in batches to threads
claims.quote: Is it not beneficial for a generic ThreadPool to support assigning tasks in batches to threads?
claims.status_note: author explained task granularity should be handled by caller before submission
claims.status_by_quote: I don't think that's thread pool responsibility. Generic thread pools are designed to execute tasks efficiently, but they don't dictate their granularity

claims.text: specifying -indexworkers=0 triggers an assertion failure in ThreadPool on startup
claims.quote: -indexworkers=0 is allowed according to the doc, but it will trigger the assert num_workers > 0 in the ThreadPool.
claims.status_note: author fixed initialization check when indexworkers is 0

claims.text: avoid std::shared_ptr and std::function overhead in ThreadPool by using std::packaged_task<void()>
claims.quote: Would be nice to avoid shared_ptr here. Apparently it is needed because std::function objects are required to be copyable and packaged tasks aren't copyable. Could fix this by avoiding std::function
claims.status_note: author adopted packaged_task<void()> wrapper in ThreadPool queue
claims.status_by_quote: ha, that's awesome... I see the trick now... That's elegant.

claims.text: extract ThreadPool into a separate pull request first
claims.quote: It could make sense to introduce the threadpool in an extra PR first, since it is very generic and can be used for multiple things
claims.status_note: author agreed to split ThreadPool to #33689 and set this PR to draft
claims.status_by_quote: will push the thread pool on an isolated PR in the coming week

claims.text: txindex parallelization causes a 3-13% slowdown on SSDs, and combining a generic shared thread pool with complex out-of-order index synchronization introduces excessive complexity
claims.quote: The txindex parallelization appears to be broken (showing 3-13% slowdowns rather than speedups)... Approach NACK from me.
claims.status_note: l0rinc reiterated deadlock and review complexity concerns after author's reply; author later agreed to split ThreadPool to #33689 and put PR into draft
claims.status_by_quote: The review effort would be the same for 2 or nproc threads, but the implications would be limited with the former

claims.text: txindex sync on SSD is ~7% slower than master due to LevelDB write contention across worker threads offsetting parallel digest gains
claims.quote: master was ~7% faster than this PR with 5 workers on an SSD. Maybe we don't enable parallel sync for txindex?
claims.status_note: author demonstrated 2.6x speedup on Signet and offered to investigate SSD slowdown or disable parallel sync for txindex
claims.status_by_quote: I'm still working on the current approach but synced the tx index on the same environment as before... Parallel Mode (5 workers): ~5 minutes... Sequential Mode: 13 minutes.
